topic.title: Contributing a Quick Fix for a Validation Problem

body.p: A plugin can contribute a custom quick fix for a validation problem.

stentry.p: Defines the fix itself. Implement two methods; two others have default implementations.
Attaches the fix to a reported problem. Returns false if the problem does not support quick fixes.

body.p: Attach it from a ValidationProblemsFilter implementation, where the plugin already receives the problems:

li.p: The contributed fix is available wherever Oxygen provides quick fixes (the quick fix menu in Text mode, the quick fix widget in Author mode, the error tooltip, and the Results view).

performFix() is invoked only when the user applies the fix. A contributed fix is never applied by the "apply all default quick fixes" feature because it can perform any action, including presenting its own user interface.

In the desktop application, performFix() runs on the AWT thread. Move long-running operations off this thread. In Web Author, the same method runs on the server while the user's request is processed. Therefore, an implementation shared by both applications must not present a user interface there.

getIconPath() accepts either a classpath-relative path or an absolute URL. For example, use the external form of a URL obtained from the plugin's class loader (jar:file:...!/images/MyFix.png). A fix with no icon uses the generic quick fix icon.

If performFix() throws an exception, Oxygen reports it to the user with the message "quick fix was not applied because it failed while performing the changes", logs the error, and does not apply anything else for that fix. In Web Author, the error is only logged.
